obligation: Banking organization notification incident (bank)
trigger: Computer-security incident that has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, the bank's ability to deliver services to a material portion of customers, or a business line whose failure would cause material loss
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the bank determines a notification incident has occurred
notify: OCC supervisory office or OCC-designated point of contact (email, telephone, or other method the OCC prescribes)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - national bank (53.1(c)). BEC against one customer: usually not. Multi-day core outage: almost certainly yes
clock_starts: Time of the recorded determination (not detection)
owner: President and CEO with the ISO and General Counsel

obligation: Banking organization notification incident (holding company)
trigger: Notification incident that affects Cris Santos Company, Inc., the bank holding company
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 36 hours after the holding company determines a notification incident has occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - U.S. bank holding company (225.300(c)); one determination record covers both companies, two notices are sent

obligation: Bank service provider notice to the bank (inbound)
trigger: Provider determines a computer-security incident has materially disrupted or degraded, or is reasonably likely to, covered services to the bank for 4 or more hours (not scheduled maintenance)
deadline: As soon as possible after the provider's determination
notify: Bank-designated point of contact (ISO and COO shared mailbox and phone); if none was given, the CEO and CIO or comparable officers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty of the 7 bank service providers; contacts given to 3 so far (POAM-015)

obligation: Bank as service provider: notice to bank respondents (outbound)
trigger: Bank determines an incident has disrupted, or is reasonably likely to disrupt, correspondent services to a bank respondent for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible after the bank's determination
notify: Each affected respondent bank's designated point of contact; if none was given, its CEO and CIO
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, per General Counsel working view that correspondent processing is a covered service (Bank Service Company Act); a legal judgment, recorded as such. Credit union respondents: per agreement
clock_starts: The bank's determination of a 4-hour disruption

obligation: Regulator notice of unauthorized access to sensitive customer information
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A II.A.1.b (guidance)
trigger: Bank becomes aware of an incident involving unauthorized access to or use of sensitive customer information (for example, a user name and password that permit access to an account)
deadline: As soon as possible
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BEC with stolen online banking credentials; core outage only if the processor reports client data access. Supplement A is interpretive guidance (should)
owner: General Counsel for the President and CEO

obligation: Customer notice under the response program
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A III.A to III.C (guidance)
trigger: Reasonable investigation shows misuse of customer information has occurred or is reasonably possible
deadline: As soon as possible; delay only if law enforcement asks in writing
notify: Affected customers (clear and conspicuous notice with the Supplement A III.B content, by mail and phone)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Chief Compliance Officer decides and documents

obligation: Service provider incident: bank remains responsible for notices
citation: 12 CFR 30 App. B, Supplement A II.A.2 (guidance)
trigger: Incident involving customer information at a service provider
deadline: Same as the bank's own notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - core processor variant; the bank cannot rely on the processor to notify its customers

obligation: Suspicious activity report
trigger: Known or suspected federal criminal violation against the bank or through it (thresholds in 21.11(c))
deadline: No later than 30 calendar days after initial detection; up to 30 more days to identify a suspect, never more than 60 days
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - BSA/AML Officer; a fraudulent wire of $25,000 or more always requires a SAR; SAR existence is confidential (21.11(k))
clock_starts: Initial detection of facts that may constitute a basis for filing

obligation: Immediate notice of an ongoing violation
trigger: A reportable violation that needs immediate attention, such as ongoing fraud
deadline: Immediately, by telephone, in addition to the timely SAR
notify: Appropriate law enforcement authority and the OCC
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the attacker is still active
clock_starts: When the ongoing violation is known

obligation: Board notice of SAR filing
trigger: A SAR is filed
deadline: Promptly after filing
notify: Board of Directors or its designated committee (Board Risk Committee)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center
trigger: Fraudulent wire from business email compromise
deadline: As soon as possible after discovery; fast reporting improves the chance of freezing funds
notify: FBI through ic3.gov; local FBI field office for large losses
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - voluntary but required by POL-03 4.10

obligation: Wire recall request to the beneficiary bank
citation: Payment system practice; funds transfer agreement (contract)
trigger: A wire the bank sent is suspected to be fraudulent
deadline: Immediately on discovery; before the beneficiary bank releases funds
notify: Beneficiary bank (phone, then written request); payment system message where available
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - not a legal notice, but the most time-critical step

obligation: Refund of an unauthorized payment order
citation: Fla. Stat. 670.202 and 670.204 (UCC Article 4A, law governing the funds transfer agreement)
trigger: A payment order accepted in the customer's name is not authorized and not effective as the customer's order, for example because the agreed security procedure was not followed
deadline: Refund with interest; General Counsel determines effectiveness
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - General Counsel decides; the callback to a number changed without verification is central

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (Florida worked example)
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(4); the law of each state where affected individuals reside
trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic personal information (includes a user name or email with a password that permits access to an online account)
deadline: Florida: no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred; notice under the primary federal regulator's rules or guidelines is deemed compliant if a copy goes to the Department on time. Other states: per each statute
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida and Georgia residents; General Counsel checks each state
clock_starts: Determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred
owner: Chief Compliance Officer with General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if 500 or more Florida individuals are affected

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Only above 1,000 individuals

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the bank (Florida)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains personal information for the bank determines a breach
deadline: Within 10 days of the agent's determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound duty of the core processor and other agents for Florida residents

obligation: Other states breach laws
trigger: Affected individuals who reside outside Florida (Georgia customers first)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators per each state law
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check residency of every affected individual

obligation: Respondent institution agreements
trigger: Disruption of correspondent services
deadline: 2019 template: no stated time; new template (2027) will state 4 hours
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, in addition to the outbound 53.4 notice

obligation: Cyber insurance and financial institution bond notice
trigger: Loss, suspected loss, or security incident
deadline: Per policy; cyber carrier hotline before hiring response vendors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal; the CFO holds the policies

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Recheck when a final rule is published

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for any bank payment (POL-03 4.12); for the processor variant, ask the processor to confirm its check

obligation: FDIC notification incident rule
trigger: Notification incident at an FDIC-supervised institution
deadline: 36 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank's primary federal regulator is the OCC (Part 53 applies instead)

obligation: Credit union reportable cyber incident
trigger: Reportable cyber incident at a federally insured credit union
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 72 hours
applies_at_this_tier: No - not a credit union (credit union respondents make their own reports)

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank is supervised by the OCC, not the FTC

obligation: NYDFS cybersecurity incident and extortion payment
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a NYDFS-regulated entity; extortion payment
deadline: 72 hours after determination; 24 hours after payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - not New York-chartered or licensed

obligation: SEC Reg S-P customer notification
trigger: Unauthorized access to sensitive customer information at a broker-dealer, investment company, investment adviser, or transfer agent
deadline: No later than 30 days after becoming aware
applies_at_this_tier: No - no SEC-registered broker-dealer or adviser

obligation: Insurance licensee cybersecurity event
citation: NAIC Model #668 sec. 6 (as adopted by states)
trigger: Cybersecurity event at an insurance licensee
deadline: 72 hours after determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - no insurance agency

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at an SEC registrant
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - both companies are privately held and are not Exchange Act reporting companies; no materiality step is needed

obligation: Covered telecommunications or Kaspersky article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the bank holds no federal contracts
